title: Republic of Pisa
capsule: The Republic of Pisa was one of the four classical Italian maritime republics, rising to commercial pre-eminence in the eleventh century through aggressive expansion in the western Mediterranean, including the suppression of Muslim piracy in Sardinia and the Balearic Islands and a prominent role in the First Crusade—Pisan ships were among those that delivered forces to Jerusalem in 1099. At its height Pisa controlled Sardinia, Corsica, and extensive trading colonies from the Levant to Catalonia. Defeat by Genoa at the Battle of Meloria in 1284 permanently shattered its naval power, and after falling under signorial rule the city was sold to the Visconti of Milan in 1399 for 200,000 gold florins, passing finally to Florence in 1406.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Pisa's Tyrrhenian core is well-attested; its transient control of Sardinia and Corsica fluctuated significantly and is known only at certain dates rather than continuously.
